paragraphs: He is mentioned in the Jerusalem Talmud, Shekalim, chapter 2, halakhah 4, but Hyman says the reading should be Rabbi Bun bar Kahana.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The proposed reading Bun bar Kahana is Hyman’s. The saved Guggenheimer digital text of Jerusalem Talmud Shekalim 2:4 also has Rabbi Bun bar Kahana.

The saved Guggenheimer Shekalim2:4 scalar explicitly has Rabbi Bun bar Kahana. It supports Rabbi in Hyman’s proposed Bun reading, whose should-be force remains explicit. Heading Bivi remains different and its abbreviation stays R'; the Bun witness does not establish a full title for Bivi. No source replacement or identity binding is made.
